gen-dafont-woodgod-gf-halant: Woodgod's tall lowercase nearly climbs to the capitals, giving the heading a stubborn, vintage swagger. Halant brings a gentler hand, with a faint thick-thin shift and outward-pointing terminals that feel like a dip pen used lightly.
gen-dafont-woodgod-gf-noto-serif-hentaig: Tall, stout and a bit old-world, Woodgod leads with wide channels into every bowl, while Noto Serif Hentaigana follows with open jaws on its curves. Both keep small letters towering.
gen-dafont-woodgod-gf-ovo: Woodgod looks commanding and vintage. Ovo sits beneath it as a serif with thins only slightly lighter than its thicks, a tall middle band, and shallow ascenders and descenders.
gen-butcherman-inter: Inter opens the pair with big, hollow counters and a smooth, tube-like look to every line. Butcherman, by contrast, shuts its letters apart with slot-like apertures, and Inter gives the dark, raw heading room to breathe.
gen-dafont-cowboys-gf-lexend-mega: Lexend Mega stands almost as tall as its capitals, with a visible gap at the end of every c. Cowboys, rustic and authoritative, spaces its stems widely and traces each line in constant width.
gen-dafont-cowboys-gf-lexend-zetta: Wide-spaced, rustic and laser-sharp, Cowboys traces every letter in a constant-width line with big gaps between stems. And Lexend Zetta, a plain sans with tall-bodied small letters and wide tracking, makes the text feel approachable.
